title: Caffeine cutoff — 8 hours before target sleep
hypothesis: Stopping caffeine at least 8 hours before target bedtime will improve subjective sleep quality over 14 days for caffeine-sensitive adults.

intervention.summary: Choose a daily caffeine cutoff clock time ~8 hours before intended sleep; switch to non-caffeine drinks after.
steps: Log all caffeine sources (coffee, tea, energy drinks, some sodas).
After cutoff, use water, herbal tea, or decaf if desired.
intervention.dose_descriptor: timing rule, not a dose recommendation

timing.phase_note: Adjust cutoff if bedtime shifts; this is a personal experiment, not medical treatment of insomnia.

expected_effect.note: Headache from reduced caffeine can occur; taper if needed and consult a clinician for dependence concerns.

stop_conditions: Clinician or pregnancy care team advises different caffeine guidance
contraindications: Medical conditions where caffeine use is clinician-directed
Eating disorder treatment plans that restrict rigid food rules without therapist support

safety.emergency_route: For emergency symptoms call local emergency services.
